did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ahithophel suggested choosing twelve thousand men and attacking David that very night, taking advantage of his exhaustion and striking him before he could organize.
Did you know? Although Ahithophel’s advice pleased Absalom and the elders of Israel, Absalom asked to hear Hushai the Archite’s advice as well.
Did you know? Hushai did not claim that David was weak. On the contrary, he described David and his men as mighty, experienced, and dangerous—like a bear robbed of her cubs in the open field.
Did you know? Instead of a small, swift attack, Hushai proposed gathering all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, in numbers as great as the sand on the seashore.
Did you know? The text explicitly states that the Lord had determined to thwart Ahithophel’s good advice in order to bring disaster upon Absalom.
Did you know? Hushai asked Zadok and Abiathar the priests to warn David not to spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but to cross the Jordan quickly.
Did you know? Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting near En Rogel because they could not risk being seen entering the city, so they received the message through a female servant.

Did you know? When Absalom’s messengers searched for Jonathan and Ahimaaz, a woman hid them in a well, spread a covering over it, and placed grain on top so that their hiding place would not be discovered.
Did you know? After the messengers delivered the warning to David, he and all his men crossed the Jordan by daybreak; not a single person was left behind.
Did you know? Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai brought David and his men abundant supplies and food at Mahanaim because the people were hungry, tired, and thirsty in the wilderness.
